subject: Post-demo cost qualification + host comparison (HealthSync)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo cost qualification + host comparison (HealthSync)

Hi Claire — thanks again for the time today, appreciate the deep dive into how HealthSync plans to use generative inference in triage and chart-summary workflows. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on pricing/next steps: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Expected call volume: ~120k patient interactions/month for pilot (text length ~1.5k tokens average), scale to ~4–7M interactions/month in year 1 production.
- Technical: mostly short-turnaround syncs (<= 1s generation target at 90th percentile) with some longer summary tasks (batch-friendly).
- Compliance: sensitive PHI; Private deployment or dedicated tenancy is likely.

Cost & pricing items I promised to capture: 
1) Pilot target volumes: you mentioned a constrained pilot budget and that procurement prefers a $/1M token view vs seat pricing.
2) Budget signal: you called out a ballpark pilot budget of $8k–$18k/month and production target budget ceiling of ~$70k/month for inference (not counting storage/infra).
3) Desired unit target: you indicated HealthSync would be happy to evaluate at a target < $10/1M tokens for any long-term provider for production (pilot flexible).

Quick benchmarking (high level):
- OpenAI (public API) — our estimate for a comparable chat+generation mix: ~ $18–$22 per 1M tokens.
- Anthropic hosted — roughly in the $12–$16 per 1M token band for the models we covered.
- Typical open-model hosts / unoptimized self-hosts — wide range, often $6–$14 per 1M depending on quantization and reserved capacity.

Questions / asks:
- Can you confirm the pilot monthly token expectation in absolute tokens (we'll convert from interactions) — you can just give a range (min/likely/max).
- Is the procurement budget you shared the total inference budget (including reserved capacity for private/dedicated), or strictly per-month variable inference spend?

Proposed next steps:
- I will pull together a short 2-option pricing sheet: (A) Pilot (no-commit, slightly higher unit) and (B) 12-month committed (volume tiers + lower $/1M).
- Schedule a 30-min procurement alignment next week to capture legal/SOC2/KMS questions.

Attached: demo deck and a small workbook where I will fill out three scenarios and host comparisons.

Thanks — feel free to reply with a precise token estimate and whether the $/1M target (< $10) is a hard constraint for shortlist.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: HealthSync-demo-deck.pdf, pilot-cost-scenarios.xlsx

From: Claire Park <claire@healthsync.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 18:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo cost qualification + host comparison (HealthSync)

Tessa — thanks for the recap and the deck. Quick answers inline below.

Pilot token estimate (high-level):
- Per interaction average: around 1.2k tokens (we re-measured after the call).
- Pilot interactions: targeting 150k interactions/month (range 100k–200k) -> ~180M tokens/month (min 120M - max 240M).

Budget clarity:
- The $8k–$18k number I gave was for the initial pilot variable spend envelope (we have separate capital reserved for any private deployment setup).
- For production (year 1 steady state), the platform team is modeling $45k–$70k/month for inference (inclusive of reserved capacity amortized).

Unit target:
- Procurement is pushing for <$10/1M tokens as the internal threshold to get to legal/engineering sign-off. If Redwood can present an offer that approaches $6–$8/1M for committed volume that will be very compelling.

One more ask: can you provide a short comparison that translates these $/1M numbers into our expected monthly spend for the ranges above? (pilot and 4M/month production scenario).

I'll also loop in procurement lead Lydia on the alignment call — copying procurement alias for scheduling.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Product Ops, HealthSync

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo cost qualification + host comparison (HealthSync)

Tessa / team — quick internal note to summarize the benchmarking and a suggested commercial path that aligns to HealthSync's asks.

Benchmarks (Redwood compiled):
- OpenAI comparable mix: $20 / 1M tokens (expected latency & feature parity).
- Anthropic comparable: $14 / 1M tokens.
- Typical open-host (managed, GPU-backed): $7.5 / 1M tokens (with committed discounts this can hit $5 / 1M).

Commercial suggestion for HealthSync:
1) Pilot (no commit): $12 / 1M tokens — gives them a price below the major hosted providers and flexibility to validate.
2) Committed volume (12 mo, annual billing) tiers:
   - Tier A: 3–6M interactions/mo approx -> $7 / 1M tokens
   - Tier B: 6–12M interactions/mo approx -> $5 / 1M tokens
   - Include a private-dedicated onboarding add-on (one-time) to cover SOC2/KMS integration.

Rationale: their procurement threshold is <$10 and they explicitly called out a $6–$8 target for committed volumes. The tiered approach hits $7 and $5 targets while keeping pilot convertible.

I'll add detailed modeled spend to the workbook (pilot and the 4M/mo scenario). Tessa — can you confirm if HealthSync prefers monthly variable billing or pre-paid committed drawdown? That will inform discount depth.

—Ben

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>

Claire / Lydia / team — thanks for the quick numbers, very helpful. I've dropped the scenario math into the attached workbook (pilot and production rows) and highlighted the $/1M conversions so you can see the monthly spend shading. TL;DR examples from the sheet: 

- Pilot (150k interactions/mo ~ 180M tokens):
  - At $12/1M -> ~$2,160/month
  - At $8/1M -> ~$1,440/month

- Production (4M interactions/mo ~ 4.8B tokens):
  - At $7/1M -> ~$33,600/month
  - At $5/1M -> ~$24,000/month

Notes: those numbers exclude one-time private/dedicated onboarding and estimated infra amortization we would include for a private deployment. I've also put two sample commercial templates in DocuSign for a pilot SOW and a 12-month committed agreement so procurement can review wording.

Next steps: 
- Can we lock a procurement call for Fri 10 Sep 2026 10:00am ET? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (SOC2 evidence, KMS & network, billing model).
- If procurement prefers, Ben will follow up with a committed-tier offer that maps to the $6–$8 target.

Claire — if you want me to re-run any of the math for different token averages (e.g., 1.0k vs 1.5k) I can do that quickly.

Best,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
